$comment: Which Poly Haven asset stands in for which piece of furniture.
This file drives the download and compression pipeline only (scripts/models.mjs). Where a
model is *placed* — the catalog keys it answers to, the yaw that turns its front to +z, how
it is fitted to the catalog's dimensions — lives in src/three/models.ts, because that is a
rendering concern and this is a build one. The `keys` below are repeated there; they are
written here so this file reads as the inventory it is, and so LICENSES.md can say what each
Every asset is CC0. `res` is the Poly Haven texture resolution to download; the pipeline
resizes to `textureSize` regardless, so 1k is plenty. `simplifyRatio` is the fraction of
vertices to keep, and is only set for the models whose polycount would otherwise dominate
the payload (the plants, which are scanned foliage).
What is *not* here matters as much as what is. Poly Haven's furniture is mostly period and
salvage: its beds are a Gothic four-poster and a rusted hospital frame, every sofa is a
Victorian settee, its desks are scratched steel, its stools are pub stools and its mirrors
are gilt. A planner for a modern rental has to look like one catalog, so those shapes keep
the procedural geometry, which is plain by construction. What survived is the short list of
assets Poly Haven itself files as `condition: clean` with modern or minimalist tags, plus
the two plants and the ottoman, whose forms carry no period at all.
